title: The Kid Who Could Hear Everyone's Thoughts
narration: On my 10th birthday, I started hearing what everyone was thinking.
At first, it was funny.
The chicken next door just thought, hm?
My teacher was thinking about pizza all day.
And my dog, ball, ball, ball, ball.
But then I went to school, hundreds of thoughts, all at once.
I'm not good enough.
Nobody likes me.
I hope she doesn't see me.
It was so loud.
I covered my ears, but I couldn't make it stop.
That evening, I walked home alone.
The sun was going down and the whole street was quiet.
Then I passed Mr. Walter's house.
He was sitting by the window like he always did.
And for the first time, I heard him.
Nobody remembers my birthday anymore.
I stopped walking.
Mr. Walter used to fix our bikes.
He gave every kid on the street candy on Halloween.
And now he was alone.
I couldn't just walk away.
So I ran.
I knocked on Mia's door, then the bakery, then the lamp shop, then every house on the street.
By the next evening, the whole town was in the square.
We hung lights from every pole.
The baker made the biggest cake I'd ever seen.
Then I knocked on Mr. Walter's door.
Can you come with me? Just for a minute.
We walked to the square.
It was completely dark.
Then the lights came on, one by one.
Surprise!
Mr. Walter didn't say anything.
His eyes filled with tears.
Then he smiled, the biggest smile I'd ever seen.
And I heard just two words.
Thank you.
I've heard a lot of thoughts since my birthday, but that was the best thought I ever heard.
